answer: Each agent identity is bound by an anchor to one pigment watermark registered in a public atlas at birth: every output it produces carries that pigment pattern, woven through its wording and structure. Peers audit the atlas at random, checking that new outputs still carry the same pigment and that no two identities share one. A forger must therefore build a full, consistent output history per fake identity, with a distinct pigment and distinct corpus each time, because a copied watermark collapses its clones into a single identity and pooled histories fail the audit.
